hints.title: Color Partition State Space
hints.text: For each distinct color i, decide how many balls k (from 0 to balls[i]) are distributed into box 1.

hints.title: Multinomial Counting Weights
hints.text: Placing k balls into box 1 contributes comb(balls[i], k) ways to the aggregate product of configurations.

hints.title: Target Verification Conditions
hints.text: Valid terminal states must have total balls in box 1 equal to n, and distinct color counts in box 1 and box 2 equal.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def getProbability(self, balls: list[int]) -> float:
        k = len(balls)
        n = sum(balls) // 2
        memo = {}
        def dfs(i, count1, d1, d2):
            if count1 > n:
                return 0, 0
            if i == k:
                if count1 == n:
                    return (1 if d1 == d2 else 0), 1
                return 0, 0
            state = (i, count1, d1, d2)
            if state in memo:
                return memo[state]
            valid_ways, total_ways = 0, 0
            b = balls[i]
            for c in range(b + 1):
                ways = math.comb(b, c)
                nd1 = d1 + (1 if c > 0 else 0)
                nd2 = d2 + (1 if b - c > 0 else 0)
                v, t = dfs(i + 1, count1 + c, nd1, nd2)
                valid_ways += v * ways
                total_ways += t * ways
            memo[state] = (valid_ways, total_ways)
            return valid_ways, total_ways
        valid, total = dfs(0, 0, 0, 0)
        return valid / total
```

variables: N: half the total number of balls
complexity.notes: Memoized state captures (color index, count of balls in box 1, distinct colors in box 1, distinct colors in box 2).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all individual ball permutations results in factorial state explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Color-wise distribution with combination weights groups identical ball permutations together.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: DFS with multinomial coefficient counting and memoization across distinct color states.
